The "Perlac Incident" was developing into open, bitter warfare. Venus remained wisely aloof, riding a crest of peace under the reign of Princess Aladdian.

arxiv-2012-00012.title: Facilitating the Communication of Politeness through Fine-Grained Paraphrasing
arxiv-2012-00012.creator: Liye Fu, Susan R. Fussell, Cristian Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil
arxiv-2012-00012.description: Abstract Aided by technology, people are increasingly able to communicate across geographical, cultural, and language barriers. This ability also results in new challenges, as interlocutors need to adapt their communication approaches to increasingly diverse circumstances. In this work, we take the first steps towards automatically assisting people in adjusting their language to a specific communication circumstance.

Our spectroscopic observations for six outbursts were performed within 1 d from their optical peak. 11 objects (TCP J00590972+3438357. arxiv-2202-03311.title: Giant topological and planar Hall effect in Cr 1/3 NbS 2
arxiv-2202-03311.creator: D. A. Mayoh, J. Bouaziz, A. E. Hall, J. B. Staunton, M. R. Lees, G. Balakrishnan
arxiv-2202-03311.description: Abstract Cr 1/3 NbS 2 is a transition metal dichalcogenide that has been of significant interest due to its ability to host a magnetic chiral soliton lattice. Conventional and planar Hall measurements provide valuable insight into the detection of exotic spin structures in chiral magnets.

arxiv-2208-03344.title: Modeling Extremal Streamflow using Deep Learning Approximations and a Flexible Spatial Process
arxiv-2208-03344.description: Abstract Quantifying changes in the probability and magnitude of extreme flooding events is key to mitigating their impacts. While hydrodynamic data are inherently spatially dependent, traditional spatial models such as Gaussian processes are poorly suited for modeling extreme events. Spatial extreme value models with more realistic tail dependence characteristics are under active development.

arxiv-2212-05974.title: Federated Few-Shot Learning for Mobile NLP CCS: Human-centered computing Ubiquitous and mobile computing CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning Conference: The 29th Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking; October 2–6, 2023; Madrid, Spain The 29th Annual Internation
arxiv-2212-05974.creator: Dongqi Cai, Shangguang Wang, Yaozong Wu, Felix Xiaozhu Lin, Mengwei Xu
arxiv-2212-05974.description: Abstract . Natural language processing (NLP) sees rich mobile applications. To support various language understanding tasks, a foundation NLP model is often fine-tuned in a federated, privacy-preserving setting (FL). This process currently relies on at least hundreds of thousands of labeled training samples from mobile clients; yet mobile users often lack willingness or knowledge to label their data.

arxiv-2306-12903.title: The limit of macroscopic homogeneous ice nucleation at the nanoscale
arxiv-2306-12903.creator: John A. Hayton, Michael B. Davies, Thomas F. Whale, Angelos Michaelides, Stephen J. Cox
arxiv-2306-12903.description: Abstract Nucleation in small volumes of water has garnered renewed interest due to the relevance of pore condensation and freezing under conditions of low partial pressures of water, such as in the upper troposphere. Molecular simulations can in principle provide insight on this process at the molecular scale that is challenging to achieve experimentally.

arxiv-2401-10817.title: A proof of the pentagon relation for skeins
arxiv-2401-10817.creator: Mingyuan Hu Department of Mathematics, Northwestern University
arxiv-2401-10817.description: Abstract . In [ HSZ23 ] , with Gus Schrader and Eric Zaslow we developed a skein-theoretic version of cluster theory, and made a conjecture on the pentagon relation for the skein dilogarithm. Here we give a topological proof of this conjecture.

arxiv-2407-17410.title: Strong Balmer break objects at z ∼ 7 − 10 z\sim 7-10 uncovered with JWST
arxiv-2407-17410.creator: A. Kuruvanthodi, D. Schaerer, R. Marques-Chaves, D. Korber, A. Weibel, P. A. Oesch, G. Roberts-Borsani
arxiv-2407-17410.description: Abstract We report the discovery of robust spectroscopically confirmed Balmer break (BB) galaxies and candidates, with secure spectroscopic redshifts 7.1 ≤ z ≤ 9.6 7.1\leq z\leq 9.6 from publicly available James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) extra-galactic photometric and spectroscopic surveys. To do so we used dedicated filters probing the Balmer break and inspected the objects with NIRSpec spectroscopy.

arxiv-2508-17023.title: Subparsec Jet Morphologies of M87 at 43 GHz: Effects of Asymmetric Plasmoids within the Jet
arxiv-2508-17023.creator: Guan-Hong Li, Hung-Yi Pu
arxiv-2508-17023.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guan-Hong Li, Hung-Yi Pu. Radio observations of the M87 jet reveal limb-brightened features that exhibit temporal variations, with the brighter limb side not remaining consistently fixed at the subparsec scales. Utilizing a force-free jet model that considers exclusively the relativistic plasma dynamics along large-scale magnetic fields attached onto the central black hole, we examine the effects of asymmetric plasmoid injections within the subparsec jet.

In agreement with previously reported structures, which were solved to a resolution of 4.4 Å, we found three types of filaments. However, our new structures, solved to a resolution of 2.

pmc-10736602.title: INTEGRATING PRIMARY CARE AND COMMUNITY-BASED PROVIDERS IN AN INTERPROFESSIONAL TEAM FOR OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10736602.creator: Denise Kropp, Danielle Clay, Susan Fosnight, Jennifer Drost, Michelle Hughes, Lorrie Warren, Jess Wilson
pmc-10736602.description: The integration of healthcare and community-based providers has been long-recognized as the gold standard in the optimal care of older adults. Social determinants of health account for more than 80% of health outcomes. Therefore, optimal care requires meaningful collaboration between medical and community-based care providers. We present here a collaborative model of care integrating community providers and healthcare system.

pmc-11753149.creator: William J. Schultz, Rosemary Ricciardeli
pmc-11753149.description: Correctional Service Providers (CSP), including Correctional officers (COs), are key front-line figures in prisons globally, with responsibility for a wide range of daily prison operations. Over the past decade, research on prison staff has massively grown. However, the portrait this scholarship draws is concerning.

pmc-12691011.title: MicroRNA-221: A Context-Dependent Mediator in Human Diseases—Highlights from Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation
pmc-12691011.creator: Qiu-Xiao Ren, Qian Zhao, Na Wu, Wanying Du, Zhaoyue Liu, Weiping J. Zhang, An-Jing Ren
pmc-12691011.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights What are the main findings? miR-221 acts as a context-dependent mediator in diverse human diseases (including cancer, cardiovascular diseases, neurological disorders, etc.) by targeting key genes (e.g., PTEN, CDKN1C/p57) and regulating conserved signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT, TGF-β/SMAD).Its function varies with disease type, cell/tissue origin, and genetic background—exerting oncogenic/tumor-suppressive effects in different cancers and protective/pathological roles in cardiovascular conditions—and it shows potential as a non-invasive biomarker for multiple diseases. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13156692.title: Longitudinal changes in coagulation-fibrinolysis in patients with traumatic brain injury within seven days after injury
pmc-13156692.creator: Xinlong Dong, Nanyu Yao, Limin Zhang, Guanghui Zheng, Yutong Zhao, Weiming Liu
pmc-13156692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryTraumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced coagulopathy is associated with poor outcomes of patients, but its progression remains poorly understood. We longitudinally collected peripheral venous blood samples from patients with TBI 24 h, 3 days, and 7 days after injury, and analyzed the samples for conventional blood and conventional coagulation tests, thromboelastography, coagulation factor activity, platelet activity, and levels of extracellular vesicles through laboratory tests.

pmc-13339451.title: Socio‐Occupational Functioning after Subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation in Parkinson's Disease
pmc-13339451.creator: Gabriele Imbalzano, Elisa Montanaro, Martina Giacchero, Claudia Ledda, Alberto Romagnolo, Mario Giorgio Rizzone, Leonardo Lopiano, Maurizio Zibetti
pmc-13339451.description: BackgroundSocio‐occupational functioning in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) treated with subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN‐DBS) is not fully captured by standard motor and quality‐of‐life scales.ObjectivesTo characterize patient‐reported socio‐occupational functioning after STN‐DBS and explore associated clinical and demographic factors.MethodsThirty‐four PD patients were assessed 9–18 months postoperatively using a semi‐structured interview covering socio‐occupational domains.

pmc-13524598.description: SummaryIntroductionThe National Infection Prevention and Control Manual (NIPCM) is an online evidence-based resource developed by Antimicrobial Resistance and Healthcare Associated Infection (ARHAI) Scotland (NHS Scotland).
